# Databases are NOT downloaded or updated implicitly during a run
# `version` is a deliberate placeholder that MUST be set to the real pinned
# version before any REAL-mode run. `version_status=unpinned` is detected and
# reported by the provenance stage; it is never silently treated as pinned.

column8: Annotation backend. `bakta_db list` reports 6.0/2025-02-24 as the only available release, and this is the edition the pilot used (docs/pilot100_pipeline_steps.md) and that 07-bakta-optimization.md, 05-cli-design.md and benchmark/bakta10.py assume. THE EDITION IS ENCODED IN database_version because the reference schema has no column for light-vs-full - a real gap, since a reader cannot otherwise tell a species-specific light database from a full one. Provision with: bakta_db download --type light --output db/bakta_db. Note this bundles AMRFinderPlus 2024-12-18.1, which AMRFinderPlus 4.2.7 rejects; bakta_db download repoints db-light/amrfinderplus-db/latest at a complete 2026-08-07.1, resolving the conflict in 07-bakta-optimization.md.

Stage 4 primary adapter. Provisioned out of band: fetch that exact directory, then build the BLAST index locally with makeblastdb -in AMRProt.fa -dbtype prot. Do NOT use amrfinder -u; it re-downloads `latest`, and an implicit mid-run update is what this project forbids. The pin is not cosmetic - config/gene_families.tsv maps this release's Class/Subclass vocabulary onto imipenem.

Typing scheme alias paeruginosa -> pseudomonas_aeruginosa is handled in config. The date is the scheme directory's own download_date, recorded because a sequence type is only reproducible against the allele set that produced it; the scheme's last_updated is 2026-03-10 and it defines 7 loci. Scheme name AND date are both in database_version because the schema has no field for either, the same gap noted on ref_bakta. Tool version pinned to the measured 2.33.1 (docs/environment-arm64.md).
Virulence database. Kept independent of the AMR stage.
Optional stage 4 adapter, disabled in config.
Core SNP alignment from the Panaroo core gene alignment.

Assembly GCF_000006765.1 version ASM676v1 (refseq NC_002516.2), 6,264,404 bp. FASTA and GFF are the SAME assembly release and were verified to match: the GFF's ##sequence-region is 'NC_002516.2 1 6264404' and the FASTA's .fai reports NC_002516.2 at 6264404 bp. Both checks were run before any coordinate from the GFF was trusted, because a silently mismatched assembly shifts every annotated gene boundary and is invisible until the biology is wrong (the failure mode a0e8bdd was written to catch for the FASTA). The GFF is used by stage 6 to resolve PAO1-coordinate variants to genes: stage 6 calls against this reference, so its coordinates are reference coordinates, NOT the assembly-local contigs Bakta reports for the cohort's own assemblies. Provisioned with: curl -sL <dir>GCF_000006765.1_ASM676v1_genomic.gff.gz then gunzip. GFF is not committed (db/ is gitignored); re-fetch with this URL and re-run both checks. Date fetched recorded here because the schema has no column for it, the same gap noted on ref_bakta and ref_mlst_pa.
